Country.evidence_source: For a study using qualitative methodology, the material comprises a relatively high number of suicides from a geographically large region in Norway constituting both urban and rural areas.

Population.evidence_source: The low proportion of women reflects the fact that suicide in the oldest age groups is genderrelated: there is a much higher incidence of suicides among men (Heisel, 2006). In 2006 in Norway the suicide rate for men over the age of 70 was 25 per 100,000 of the population, while for women in the same age group it was 3 (Statistics Norway, 2008).

Type.evidence_source: The suicides were reported regularly by the registration body in the municipalities with no selection other than absolute certainty that the cause of death was suicide. The entire age range from 65 to 90 is represented. ... According to the suicide figures from the region in question in 2006, almost half the suicides were reported to the project (Statistics Norway, personal communication).

Area.evidence_source: The low proportion of women reflects the fact that suicide in the oldest age groups is genderrelated: there is a much higher incidence of suicides among men (Heisel, 2006). ... Norwegian women more often choose methods that provide a higher chance of survival (poisoning), while men use those that are more certain to lead to death (Kjølseth et al., 2002). ... It is possible that not only gender but also personality traits are decisive for choice of method. This may thus restrict the transferability of our findings to elderly people who choose violent methods of suicide.
